title: Remapping shortcut not working in edge

status.label: Needs mapping details
status.detail: The 0.69.1 report describes overlapping global and Edge-specific mappings, but it does not clearly identify the physical source key, mapped output, or which shortcut fails today.

next_action: Request the exact current mapping entries and a current-version reproduction before choosing an implementation path.

judgment.rationale: The report gives an old 0.69.1 configuration involving an Edge-specific shortcut and a global shortcut, but its description of pressing PrintScreen and the resulting sequence is ambiguous; there are no comments confirming current behavior. Current main selects an app-specific remap table when the activated application is resolved and otherwise falls back to the OS-level table, but the report does not identify whether Edge detection, mapping direction, or a key conflict is failing.
evidence: The issue is open, unassigned, has no public comments, and is labeled Issue-Bug and Product-Keyboard Manager.

The body lists PowerToys 0.69.1 and describes a Right Ctrl+Right Shift+S / PrintScreen mapping targeted at msedge alongside a global Win+Left Shift+S mapping, but the stated keypress/result direction is unclear.
The 2026-10-11 issue activity is a product-label change; it adds no new reproduction or author confirmation.

At upstream main 0b1dd814878f0dfbb07787d9c3e52a2897b6f769, KeyboardManagerEngineLibrary/State.cpp:122-134 selects the app-specific shortcut map when an activated app name is present and otherwise returns the OS-level map.
A direct pull-request search for this issue returned no linked PR.
judgment.recommended_action: Request a current-build reproduction and the exact source, mapped-to, and target-app values for both mappings.

fix_assessment.rationale: A code change is plausible if the app-specific mapping is not selected or a collision with the global mapping changes the result, but the old report does not unambiguously state which input is pressed or what output is expected.

issue_context.summary: An old Keyboard Manager report describes an Edge-specific shortcut mapping overlapping a global mapping, but the exact input and output sequence is ambiguous and has not been confirmed on a current build.
known_information: The body lists PowerToys 0.69.1 and says Right Ctrl+Right Shift+S is mapped to PrintScreen for msedge, while Win+Left Shift+S is also mapped to PrintScreen globally.
The body says pressing PrintScreen in Edge produces Win+Left Shift+S, but does not clearly state which mapping direction or physical sequence was intended.
There are no public comments or assignees; the October 2026 activity changes product labeling only.
Current main has app-specific and OS-level shortcut remap tables; app-specific selection depends on an activated application name.
inferences: A mapping-precedence or foreground-application resolution issue is possible, but the old configuration could also be misunderstood or obsolete.
The app-specific map selection path is relevant, but current source alone does not demonstrate a defect.
issue_context.analysis: The issue is unassigned, so the previous ownership status was incorrect. The old report needs a screenshot/export of both mappings and a current-version reproduction that distinguishes the physical source key from the mapped output. Until that is available, a code design would risk solving the wrong mapping direction.
initial_investigation: Read the live issue body, labels, assignees, comments, and timeline through 2026-10-11T16:49:00Z; the latest timeline change is only a product-label update.
Checked for a directly linked pull request; none was returned by the issue-number search.

information_gaps.information: A numbered current-build sequence stating which physical keys are pressed and the expected and actual output in Edge and outside Edge.

proposed_fixes.title: Resolve app-specific shortcut mappings consistently in Edge
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: the Edge-specific mapping may not be selected when the foreground process is resolved, or the overlapping global and app-specific mappings may be interpreted as a chained remap. The report is too ambiguous and old to distinguish these causes.
plan: Capture both current mapping entries with their source shortcut, mapped output, and target application, and reproduce on a current supported build.
Trace the foreground application name and selected mapping table for the exact physical key sequence.
If the current app-specific mapping is bypassed or collides with the global mapping, correct table selection/precedence and add a focused regression test.
verification: The reported source shortcut produces the configured output in Edge on a current supported build.
The global Win+Left Shift+S mapping continues to work outside Edge, and unrelated Edge shortcuts remain unchanged.

confidence.rationale: Current code contains separate app-specific and OS-level tables, but the issue has no recent reproduction or comments and does not clearly describe mapping direction.

comment.body:
The report describes an Edge-specific Right Ctrl+Right Shift+S mapping and a global Win+Left Shift+S mapping, but it is unclear which physical keys you press and which mapped output is expected. If this still occurs on a current PowerToys build, could you share:
- Only those two mapping rows (source, mapped-to, target app), and whether the target is msedge.exe.
- Numbered steps with the physical keys pressed and expected/actual output in Edge and a non-Edge app.
- Current PowerToys and Windows versions. Unrelated settings are not needed.

actions.label: Approve app-specific mapping investigation
actions.note: Start a code investigation only after the current mapping directions and reproduction are clear.
